title: Fair Finetuning Mitigates Distribution Inference Attacks
abstract: Machine learning models trained on sensitive data can inadvertently leak population-level information about their training distributions -- a threat known as distribution inference attack (DIA). An adversary with black-box access can infer sensitive demographic properties, such as subgroup proportions, without observing any training data directly. While defenses such as differential privacy and property unlearning have been proposed, the link between fairness constraints and distributional leakage remains unexplored. We propose Fair Fine-tuning (FFt): a trained model is fine-tuned on samples from the complementary distribution under an Equalized Odds (EO) constraint. We provide a complete theoretical characterization, proving the tight bound $\text{Adv}(\mathcal{A},M_f) \le Δ_{\text{EO}} \cdot W$, where $W$ quantifies how distinguishable the two training distributions are by their sensitive-attribute composition. We also establish a necessary condition for FFt to reduce adversarial advantage and prove tightness of the bound. We evaluate across six datasets spanning tabular (ACS Income, COMPAS, German Credit), image (UTKFaces), and NLP (Bias in Bios) modalities. Rehearsal-based FFt consistently reduces the adversarial accuracy gap below the detection threshold $τ!=!0.1$ across all settings; on ACS Income, the gap falls from $\sim!15%$ to under $4%$. Our work provides the first formal bound connecting a model's measured EO disparity directly to its adversarial advantage in the DIA game, opening a new avenue for unified fairness-and-privacy defenses.

title: Composition Theorems for Multiple Differential Privacy Constraints
abstract: The exact composition of mechanisms for which two differential privacy (DP) constraints hold simultaneously is studied. The resulting privacy region admits an exact representation as a mixture over compositions of mechanisms of heterogeneous DP guarantees, yielding a framework that naturally generalizes to the composition of mechanisms for which any number of DP constraints hold. This result is shown through a structural lemma for mixtures of binary hypothesis tests. Lastly, the developed methodology is applied to approximate $f$-DP composition.

title: Blind Identification of Channel Codes: A Subspace-Coding Approach
abstract: The problem of blind identification of channel codes at a receiver involves identifying a code chosen by a transmitter from a known code-family, by observing the transmitted codewords through the channel. Most existing approaches for code-identification are contingent upon the codes in the family having some special structure, and are often computationally expensive otherwise. Further, rigorous analytical guarantees on the performance of these existing techniques are largely absent. This work presents a new method for code-identification on the binary symmetric channel (BSC), inspired by the framework of subspace codes for operator channels, carefully combining principles of hamming-metric and subspace-metric decoding. We refer to this method as the minimum denoised subspace discrepancy decoder. We present theoretical guarantees for code-identification using this decoder, for bounded-weight errors, and also present a bound on the probability of error when used on the BSC. Simulations demonstrate the improved performance of our decoder for random linear codes beyond existing general-purpose techniques, across most channel conditions and even with a limited number of received vectors.

title: Advancing Text Classification with Large Language Models and Neural Attention Mechanisms
abstract: This study proposes a text classification algorithm based on large language models, aiming to address the limitations of traditional methods in capturing long-range dependencies, understanding contextual semantics, and handling class imbalance. The framework includes text encoding, contextual representation modeling, attention-based enhancement, feature aggregation, and classification prediction. In the representation stage, deep semantic embeddings are obtained through large-scale pretrained language models, and attention mechanisms are applied to enhance the selective representation of key features. In the aggregation stage, global and weighted strategies are combined to generate robust text-level vectors. In the classification stage, a fully connected layer and Softmax output are used to predict class distributions, and cross-entropy loss is employed to optimize model parameters. Comparative experiments introduce multiple baseline models, including recurrent neural networks, graph neural networks, and Transformers, and evaluate them on Precision, Recall, F1-Score, and AUC. Results show that the proposed method outperforms existing models on all metrics, with especially strong improvements in Recall and AUC. In addition, sensitivity experiments are conducted on hyperparameters and data conditions, covering the impact of hidden dimensions on AUC and the impact of class imbalance ratios on Recall. The findings demonstrate that proper model configuration has a significant effect on performance and reveal the adaptability and stability of the model under different conditions. Overall, the proposed text classification method not only achieves effective performance improvement but also verifies its robustness and applicability in complex data environments through systematic analysis.

title: SelfCheck-Eval: A multi-module framework for zero-resource hallucination detection in large language models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved considerable progress across diverse applications, yet their tendency to generate incorrect or fabricated content, commonly termed hallucinations, remains a fundamental obstacle to reliable deployment in high-stakes domains. Existing detection benchmarks are confined to general-knowledge settings, leaving specialized fields, where accuracy is important, underexplored. To address this gap, we introduce the American Invitational Mathematics Examination (AIME) Math Hallucination dataset, a benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning hallucinations, and propose SelfCheck-Eval, an LLM-agnostic, black-box detection framework compatible with open- and closed-source LLMs. The framework integrates three independent modules, semantic, specialized detection, and contextual consistency, into a suitable architecture. Systematic evaluation reveals a noticeable performance gap: existing methods perform well on biographical content but struggle with mathematical reasoning, a deficit that continues across natural language inference (NLI) fine-tuning, preference learning, and process supervision paradigms. These findings expose fundamental limitations of current approaches and motivate the development of specialized, black-box-compatible methods for trustworthy LLM deployment.

evidence.title: SelfCheckAgent: Zero-Resource Hallucination Detection in Generative Large Language Models
evidence.abstract: Detecting hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs) remains a critical challenge for their reliable deployment in real-world applications. To address this, we introduce SelfCheckAgent, a novel framework integrating three different agents: the Symbolic Agent, the Specialized Detection Agent, and the Contextual Consistency Agent. These agents provide a robust multi-dimensional approach to hallucination detection. Notable results include the Contextual Consistency Agent leveraging Llama 3.1 with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) to achieve outstanding performance on the WikiBio dataset, with NonFactual hallucination detection scoring 93.64%, Factual 70.26%, and Ranking 78.48% respectively. On the AIME dataset, GPT-4o with CoT excels in NonFactual detection with 94.89% but reveals trade-offs in Factual with 30.58% and Ranking with 30.68%, underscoring the complexity of hallucination detection in the complex mathematical domains. The framework also incorporates a triangulation strategy, which increases the strengths of the SelfCheckAgent, yielding significant improvements in real-world hallucination identification. The comparative analysis demonstrates SelfCheckAgent's applicability across diverse domains, positioning it as a crucial advancement for trustworthy LLMs. These findings highlight the potentiality of consistency-driven methodologies in detecting hallucinations in LLMs.

title: Natural Language Processing and Machine Learning Models for Classifying and Predicting Graft Loss after Kidney Transplantation
abstract: **Antecedentes:** La identificación confiable de la pérdida del injerto renal y la estratificación oportuna del riesgo siguen siendo desafíos en la práctica clínica rutinaria, particularmente en contextos donde las variables de los registros son incompletas y la codificación mediante CIE es inconsistente. Esta tesis abordó estas brechas mediante el aprovechamiento de historias clínicas electrónicas en español y el desarrollo de herramientas predictivas con riesgos competitivos, alineadas con puntos clave de decisión a lo largo del proceso de trasplante. **Métodos:** Se realizaron tres estudios de cohorte retrospectivos en Colombiana de Trasplantes, Colombia. El Estudio 1 desarrolló modelos de procesamiento de lenguaje natural y aprendizaje automático supervisado para clasificar el estado del injerto a partir de texto clínico no estructurado en español, incluyendo 2.712 receptores, 117.566 documentos y el periodo 2008–2023. Se utilizaron normalización y tokenización del texto, submuestreo, selección de características mediante LASSO y validación cruzada de 10 iteraciones para comparar regresión logística, Random Forest y redes neuronales. El Estudio 2 desarrolló y validó internamente una calculadora pretrasplante para predecir la pérdida del injerto durante el primer año, utilizando únicamente variables disponibles en el momento de la oferta del donante, es decir, la información disponible cuando se ofrece un órgano y se debe tomar una decisión de aceptación o rechazo antes del trasplante. Este estudio incluyó 2.030 receptores entre 2008 y 2023, y comparó un Random Survival Forest para riesgos competitivos frente a una regresión de Fine–Gray. La discriminación, calibración y el análisis de curvas de decisión se evaluaron mediante validación cruzada estratificada. El Estudio 3 desarrolló un modelo pronóstico temprano postrasplante basado en Random Survival Forest para riesgos competitivos, en receptores vivos y con injerto funcional a los 30 ± 7 días después del trasplante. Este estudio incluyó 2.077 receptores entre 2008 y 2024, utilizando predictores clínicos, quirúrgicos, infecciosos e histopatológicos del primer mes, así como validación cruzada estratificada de 10 iteraciones. **Resultados:** En el Estudio 1, el modelo Random Forest alcanzó el mayor AUC en el conjunto de prueba, con un valor de 0,98, y el mayor puntaje F1, con un valor de 0,65. La sensibilidad fue de 0,76 y el valor predictivo positivo de 0,56, lo que refleja una alta capacidad de discriminación, aunque con falsos positivos persistentes en un contexto de clases desbalanceadas. En el Estudio 2, el modelo Random Survival Forest para riesgos competitivos superó al modelo de Fine–Gray, con un índice C de 0,87 frente a 0,72. Además, mostró una alta sensibilidad, del 88%, una excelente identificación de candidatos de bajo riesgo, con un valor predictivo negativo del 98%, y un beneficio neto positivo en el análisis de curvas de decisión. En el Estudio 3, la incidencia acumulada al primer año fue de 7,3% para pérdida del injerto y de 1,8% para muerte con injerto funcional. El modelo Random Survival Forest para riesgos competitivos alcanzó un índice C de 0,75 y, con un umbral de riesgo de 0,08, obtuvo una sensibilidad de 92,3% y un valor predictivo negativo de 99,3%. La tasa de filtración glomerular estimada al día 30 fue el predictor dominante. **Conclusiones:** En conjunto, estos estudios muestran que las historias clínicas electrónicas no estructuradas en español pueden apoyar la identificación escalable del desenlace de estado del injerto, y que los modelos de aprendizaje automático con riesgos competitivos pueden proporcionar una estratificación de riesgo clínicamente útil tanto en el momento de la oferta del donante como durante el seguimiento temprano postrasplante. Los trabajos futuros deben enfocarse en la validación temporal y externa, así como en la evaluación prospectiva del impacto clínico.

title: 基于"人工智能+教育"的物联网专业单片机技术教学改革
abstract: 人工智能与教育深度融合、新工科建设蓬勃开展,单片机技术作为物联网工程专业的核心课程,其传统教学模式存在内容更新滞后、实践与产业脱节、个性化教学不够充分、考核方式单一诸种问题,因而不能很好地满足智能物联网时代人才培养的需要。因此本文以广东科技学院物联网工程专业为研究对象,以"人工智能+教育"理念为基本出发点,从教学内容重构、教学模式创新、实践体系优化、考核评价改革四个维度系统、有层次地推进单片机技术教学改革,又依托超星学习通平台搭建数字化教学平台,将虚拟仿真技术与项目式教学自然、妥帖地结合,把人工智能基础算法、智能物联网应用场景、单片机实践三者有机融合,形成分层递进、逻辑清晰的混合式教学体系。实践结果也十分明确地证明,改革切实提高了学生的实践动手能力、创新思维能力和工程素养,故而对地方本科院校物联网及电子信息类专业课程改革有极好的示范意义。

title: Memclave: Secure In-Memory Enclave for Untrusted Hosts
abstract: We present Memclave, a software-only framework that brings code integrity and data confidentiality to commodity PIM without hardware changes. A TPM-attested hypervi- sor permanently isolates the PIM’s control plane from host access at boot. On each in-memory core, a trusted loader authenticates the user kernel and establishes a per-session protected data path. Memclave preserves the programming model and kernel code: host applications replace a small set of data-movement calls with secure drop-ins, keeping the trusted computing base small and porting effort low. We implement Memclave on off-the-shelf UPMEM DIMMs and evaluate it across the PrIM benchmark suite, covering heterogeneous memory-access, compute, and synchronization patterns. After a one-time ∼100 ms authenticated load, in-memory kernel time remains close to the PIM baseline: Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) stays within 1.5× at practical sizes, and Breadth–First Search (BFS) is 1.1× on some graphs with modest rise as number of frontier levels increase.

title: Bayesian Inference for Crop Classification Models
abstract: This study introduces a random walk based greedy algorithm with stochastic updates for interpreting black-box machine learning model. A Bayesian hierarchical probabilistic surrogate model was formulated to quantify the uncertainty of the latent parameters of the machine learning model using a hyper-prior. Bayesian credible intervals were obtained to determine the significance of each parameter. Furthermore, the proposed algorithm is compared with the standard logistic regression surrogate model. The algorithm simulation performance was tested using Crop Recommendation based on Soil Properties and Weather Prediction Dataset.. KEYWORDS :Random walk, Stochastic update, Bayesian surrogate model, Interpreting machine learning, Precision agriculture.

title: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF QUANTUM CRYPTOGRAPHY: PRINCIPLES, PROTOCOLS, AND PRACTICAL CHALLENGES
abstract: The quantum cryptography approach is a significant change in secure communication in the sense that quantum cryptography bases its security on the law of quantum physics as opposed to computation difficulty. With classical encryption methods rapidly losing their resistance to the power of the underlying computers as well as the expected possibilities of the quantum computers, quantum cryptography comes into the limelight as a possible method of securing information in the long term. The paper is a detailed and systematic review of quantum cryptography along with the fundamentals of this practice, the way it works, and its practical implementation. It describes the ability of quantum phenomena to be unique (including superposition, uncertainty, and disturbance of measurement) and able to secure a key exchange as well as ensure any attempt of eavesdropping would be automatically noticed.In the review, the authors mainly discuss quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols, their functioning principles, security assurances, and the benefits of quantum over classical key exchange schemes. Besides that, the paper critically evaluates the real issues surrounding the implementation of quantum cryptographic systems such as hardware limitations, transmission range, environmental noise, and compatibility, to existing compatibility infrastructures. Recent advances in the field of experiments and pilot implementations are presented to determine the maturity of new technologies, and their suitability to be used on a large scale. Through its analytical review of theoretical assets, as well as practical constraints, this paper offers a definite and equalist view of the state of quantum cryptography today and also explains the research priorities important in its scale, moving away of the test production systems to the dependable and extensive security measures.

title: BIAS DETECTION AND FAIRNESS ANALYSIS IN LOAN APPROVAL PROCESS USING XAI
abstract: AI is now being used everywhere in banks, especially to decide who gets a loan and who doesn't. This makes things much faster and more accurate. But there is a problem: these AI models are like "black boxes," meaning we don't know how they make decisions. This can lead to unfairness, or bias. In this project, we built a system using Explainable AI to find and fix bias in loan approvals. We used tools called SHAP and LIME[1][2] to look at a loan dataset and check if there was any unfairness based on gender. We also tested if our explanations were reliable. Our results showed that the AI was a bit biased against women (especially those with high debt), but by using XAI, we were able to spot this and reduce the bias by 20-30%[20][21]. This shows that XAI is really important for making AI fair and trustworthy in the real world.

title: INTEGRATING MACHINE LEARNING INTO WEB APPLICATIONS
abstract: The integration of Machine Learning (ML) into web applications has transformed the way modern digital platforms interact with users and process data. By incorporating intelligent algorithms into web-based systems, developers can create applications that learn from user behavior, automate decision-making, and provide personalized experiences. This paper explores the methodologies, tools, and frameworks used to integrate machine learning models into web applications. It discusses the architecture of ML-powered web systems, including data collection, model training, deployment, and real-time prediction. Popular technologies such as Python, TensorFlow, Scikit-learn, Flask, Django, and cloud-based services are examined for their roles in facilitating seamless integration. The study also highlights practical applications, including recommendation systems, chatbots, fraud detection, sentiment analysis, and predictive analytics. Furthermore, it addresses key challenges such as scalability, model performance, security, data privacy, and maintenance. By analyzing current trends and best practices, this research demonstrates how machine learning enhances the functionality, efficiency, and user engagement of web applications. The findings emphasize that successful integration requires a balance between robust machine learning models and efficient web development practices. As artificial intelligence continues to evolve, the adoption of ML-driven web applications is expected to grow, offering innovative solutions across various industries and improving overall user experiences.

title: AI-Driven Neuromarketing and Sustainable Business Outcomes: The Role of Emotional Engagement and Purchase Decision Influence
abstract: Consumer responses to marketing stimuli are increasingly shaped by AI-driven personalisation systems that engage affective processing pathways before deliberate evaluation occurs.This study examines how perceived AI-neuromarketing stimuli influence emotional engagement and purchase decision-making, and whether these constructs jointly predict sustainable business outcomes among consumers.A cross-sectional survey was administered to 218 respondents using stratified purposive sampling.The data were analysed through one-way ANOVA, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression.Emotional engagement varied significantly across age groups, with younger consumers demonstrating markedly higher affective responsiveness than older cohorts.The regression model revealed that AI-neuromarketing stimulus perception, emotional engagement, and purchase decision influence collectively explained 54.8% of variance in sustainable business outcomes.These findings extend Stimulus-Organism-Response theory to AI-mediated consumer contexts and offer empirically grounded strategic guidance for businesses targeting demographically diverse Indian markets.

title: Marathi Grammar Error Correction Using Fine-Tuned IndicBART for Low-Resource Language Processing
abstract: Grammar Error Correction (GEC) is an essential problem in the Natural Language Processing (NLP) domain where the objective is to detect and automatically correct the grammatical mistakes present in any piece of text.Though there have been many advanced grammar correction models developed for high resource languages like English, robust grammar correction tools are yet to be created for regional Indian languages.The Indo-Aryan language, Marathi, poses distinct challenges in grammar correction owing to its heavy morphology, gender based verb agreement, complex sentence structure, and dependencies on context.This work introduces MarathiGEC, a transformer based Marathi Grammar Error Correction tool using the IndicBART model.An annotated corpus of sentence pairs which contain grammatically wrong sentences and their corrections in Marathi language were created to train the IndicBART model.The presented GEC model uses a sequence to sequence text generation method and thus can correct grammatical errors in the context of their meaning.Experimentation proves the effectiveness of the model to correct errors in gender agreement, verb conjugation, tense consistency, misspellings, and sentence structure..

title: Provenance-Tracked Concept Directional Substitution: Lineage-Sourced Replacement Vectors for Auditable Model Editing
abstract: PT-CDS extends mean-difference abliteration with lineage-sourced replacement directions and a cryptographically hashed audit ledger. Revision 2: §2.2 now requires the substitution direction to be orthogonal to the removed direction (⟨d_sub, d⟩ = 0), enforced by a Gram–Schmidt step. A proof is provided that without this orthogonalization the substitution silently re-introduces a component of the abliterated concept proportional to substitution_scale · |⟨d_sub, d⟩|. The config flag orthogonalize_substitution=True is now the default. The concept_edit_ledger records substitute_orthogonalized: true to confirm the condition was enforced.

title: Semi-Supervised Multi-View Graph Anomaly Detection with Limited Labeled Data
abstract: This report synthesises findings from 12 peer-reviewed papers addressing the following research question: How does the sample efficiency of semi-supervised multi-view graph anomaly detection frameworks compare to single-view methods when trained with less than 5\% labeled anomalous nodes. Deep convolutional neural networks have performed remarkably well on many Computer Vision tasks. However, these networks are heavily reliant on big data to avoid overfitting. 9 claims were extracted from source literature; 9 were independently verified against retrieved documents. title: Reply on RC1-RC3
abstract: Abstract. This study proposes a method to enhance neural network performance when training data and application data are not very similar, e.g., out of distribution problems, as well as pattern and regime shifts. The method consists of three main steps: 1) Retrain the neural network towards reasonable subsets of the training data set and note down the resulting weight anomalies. 2) Choose reasonable predictors and derive a regression between the predictors and the weight anomalies. 3) Extrapolate the weights, and thereby the neural network, to the application data. We show and discuss this method in three nonlinear use cases from the climate sciences, which include successful temporal, spatial and cross-domain extrapolations of neural networks.

title: Design Objectives and Requirements for a PI Dynamic Interoperability Tool
abstract: Digital interoperability remains a critical barrier to realizing the Physical Internet (PI) vision, as heterogeneous information systems across logistics stakeholders prevent seamless, dynamic data exchange. Traditional approaches such as static standards and bilateral mappings fail to scale in decentralized networks with diverse, evolving data models and dynamic interoperability requirements. This paper develops design objectives and requirements for a PI Dynamic Interoperability Tool (PIDIT) that leverages large language models (LLMs) for semantic interoperability. Following the echelon-based design science research (eDSR) methodology, we first establish the problem through a literature review and validate it with nine semi-structured expert interviews, identifying 77 problems aggregated into 14 interrelated meta problems. A subsequent review of LLM-based interoperability research across ontology matching, schema matching, semantic translation, and knowledge graph construction confirms that no existing approach fully addresses the PI's runtime interoperability needs. Building on these foundations, we formulate five design objectives and associated design requirements, ranging from semantic understanding of heterogeneous formats to autonomous interoperability at scale with human-in-the-loop oversight. This work provides a rigorously validated problem-requirements foundation for subsequent design and evaluation of the PIDIT.

title: Disentangled Graph Representation Based on Prototype Subgraph Neural Network
abstract: While graph representation learning methods have been successfully applied to various graph data mining tasks, they typically couple graph information into an unstructured holistic representation. This makes it difficult to explicitly identify substructures with specific functionalities within the graph and lacks the ability to mine discriminative prototype structures that can be shared across graphs. To address these challenges, this paper proposes Prototype Subgraph Disentangled Graph Neural Network (PSDGNN). It explicitly disentangles node features into multiple independent latent factor groups through latent factor decomposition and prototype alignment mechanisms. A subgraph generator then converts these factors into factor subgraphs to model latent semantic substructures. Furthermore, learnable prototype subgraphs are introduced to represent foundational structural patterns shared across graphs. Through similarity matching and mutual information minimization objectives, the model aligns factor subgraphs with corresponding prototypes in structural semantics. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance over existing baseline methods across seven public datasets. The model provides intuitive, structured explanations for classification decisions through visualizable factor subgraphs and prototype subgraphs, significantly enhancing interpretability and generalization capabilities.

title: A Level-Direction Guided Hierarchical Particle Swarm Optimization for Wind Farm Layout Optimization
abstract: Abstract Wind Farm Layout Optimization Problem (WFLOP) aims to optimize turbine placement to mitigate wake-effect losses and improve power generation efficiency. Existing particle swarm optimization (PSO)-based approaches for WFLOP mainly rely on conventional variants and lack problem-specific search mechanisms. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a level-direction guided hierarchical particle swarm optimization algorithm (HGPSO). The proposed method integrates multi-direction guidance and hierarchical learning to enhance population diversity and convergence performance. Comprehensive experiments under various wind conditions, turbine scales, and land constraints show that HGPSO outperforms several state-of-the-art WFLOP optimizers in most test cases, achieving average improvements of approximately 0.5%–3.0% in energy conversion efficiency. Statistical tests further confirm its robustness and stability. The proposed HGPSO provides an effective and scalable solution for complex wind farm layout optimization.

title: Hardware-efficient photonic neural network processor by mode-division multiplexing
abstract: In this study, we propose and demonstrate a hardware-efficient photonic neural network processor utilizing low-rank approximation (LRA) in conjunction with mode-division multiplexing (MDM) techniques. By exploiting MDM, the architecture requires only a single optical source, substantially reducing the hardware complexity associated with multi-source systems. Through LRA, the proposed architecture integrates two single-mode Mach-Zehnder interferometers (MZIs) and four mode-insensitive MZIs to construct a 4 × 2 matrix with the rank of 1. Compared to previously photonic neural network processors employing MZIs or microring resonators (MRRs), our approach achieves a 25% reduction in the number of optical components through LRA for the 4 × 2 matrix configuration. Fabricated on an 800 nm silicon nitride platform, the MDM-enabled LRA photonic neural network processor was experimentally validated on a facial expression recognition task and achieved a prediction accuracy of 96% on the MNIST dataset. Our work provides a scalable and hardware-efficient pathway toward photonic matrix operations, particularly well-suited for resource-constrained applications.

title: Optimal Control Problem and Symbolic Regression for Solving It in the Class of Practically Realizable Functions
abstract: Abstract The optimal control problem is considered. Its solution is sought in the class of functions that can be implemented on the onboard processor of the controlled plant. First, the problem of synthesizing a universal motion stabilization system is solved. To this end, a set of possible trajectories and a set of initial states are specified, and a single universal system is constructed that stabilizes the motion of the plant along all the given trajectories from all the given initial states. To obtain a mathematical expression for the function of the universal stabilization system, the method of symbolic regression is employed. A new symbolic regression technique, the universal code, is described; it combines all the advantages of well-known symbolic regression methods, genetic programming, Cartesian genetic programming, and the network operator method. After synthesizing the motion stabilization system, the optimal control problem is solved. A reference model is introduced into the plant control system, and the optimal control problem is solved for this model in the classical formulation. The reference model generates an optimal trajectory, while the universal stabilization system ensures high-quality motion of the plant in the vicinity of that trajectory. An example of solving the optimal control problem by the proposed method for a group of two quadcopters is presented.
